title: Answering and bouncing it back: bien, ¿y tú?
note: Always return the question and mirror tú / usted (¿Cómo está usted? → Y usted, ¿cómo está?). Regular = so-so, a false friend.

title: How do you spell it?: ¿cómo se escribe?

forms.en: Could you spell it for me, please? (formal)

note: Deletrear = to spell out.

title: How's it going? (Colombian): ¿qué más?

forms.en:
How's it going, how are you doing?
Fine, and you?

note: Everyday Colombian greeting; it doesn't ask for news.

title: What does it mean?: ¿qué significa…?
note: Pairs with ¿Cómo se dice…?. Trancón = traffic jam (Colombian).

title: Sorry? Could you say that again?: ¿me repite?
en: Could you say that again, please? (formal)

forms.en: Could you say that again, please? (formal)

note: A bare ¿Qué? sounds rude; ¿Cómo? or ¿Perdón? is polite. ¿Me repite? is very Colombian. Spain's Perdona, no te he entendido → Perdón, no le entendí.

title: That's very kind: muy amable
en: That's very kind of you, thanks.

forms.en: That's very kind of you, thanks.

note: To a stranger who has helped you.

title: Right?: ¿no?, ¿cierto?, ¿verdad?
note: Tags ask for agreement, not information. ¿Cierto? is very Colombian.

title: My pleasure (Colombian 'you're welcome'): con mucho gusto
note: The usual Colombian reply to gracias; de nada works everywhere. Not the same as mucho gusto (nice to meet you).

title: Hey, what's up? (Colombian street greeting): ¿quiubo?
note: Story dialogue / recognition: very informal Colombian (from ¿qué hubo?). Parce = mate, strongly regional slang.

title: Have you got it? (tener with everyone)
note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): tener's present for every person before the boot verbs (22) explain it; tengo is c:tengo (session 3). Frame: ¿Tienes…? / ¿Tiene…? / Tenemos… / Tienen…

title: His name is…, what's it called?: se llama

forms.en: Their names are Ana and Luis.

note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): talking about other people's names (mi hermana se llama Ana) long before reflexives (76). Frame: Se llama… / ¿Cómo se llama? / Se llaman…

title: What's this?: ¿qué es esto?
note: Neuter esto / eso until it has a name, then este / esta: este colador. The answer keeps its article (*Es colador).

title: It's open, it's closed
note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): survival: shops, the café, the bank. abierto is a participle, so it would otherwise wait for g:estar-participle (136).

title: I'm going, are you going?: voy, vas
note: Pull-forward pass (Oct 2026): ir is a top-30 verb and u02 is the day-to-day unit (voy al café a las seis); the system arrives with g:ir-a-plans (26). Frame: Voy… / ¿Vas…?

forms.en: What do you do for a living?
What do you do for a living? (formal)
What do you do for work?

note: ¿Qué haces? can be answered with a hobby or with what you're doing now; these ask about work.

title: Sure, let's go!: ¡de una!
en:
Shall we go to the cinema?
Absolutely!
note: Colombian, informal: an immediate, enthusiastic yes. Source lesson is A2; taught at A1 here.

title: I don't mind: me da igual
en:
Tea or coffee?
I don't mind.

forms.en:
Tea or coffee?
I don't mind.

note: Fine among friends; to a host, Cualquiera está bien, gracias is warmer. Source lesson is A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Cool!: ¡qué chévere!
note: Widely understood in LatAm; very Colombian. Spain's guay is not used. Source lesson is A2; taught at A1 here.

title: See you on Monday: hasta el lunes
note: hasta el + day (*hasta lunes). Naming the next meeting is warmer than a bare chao.

forms.es: No me gusta nada el frío.
forms.en: I don't like the cold at all.

note: No before the verb, nada after it: the strong no. Odio is stronger still.

title: What do you like doing?: ¿qué te gusta hacer?

What do you do at weekends?

note: Gustar + infinitive stays singular: me gusta leer y escribir. Source lesson is A2; taught at A1 here.

note: Commands used as attention-getters (oiga = usted, oye = tú). Oiga alone can sound abrupt; stack it with disculpe. Mira / mire work the same way. Source lesson is A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Watch out!: ¡ojo!
note: Colombian ojo = watch out. No dar papaya (don't make yourself an easy target): recognition. Source lesson is A2; taught at A1 here.

title: Getting attention: oye, mira, dime
en: Hey, have you got a minute?

forms.en: Hey, have you got a minute?

forms.es: Mira, el problema es que no tengo plata.
forms.en: Look, the problem is I haven't got any money.

note: Usted: oiga, mire, dígame (also on the phone). Fillers, not real commands. Source lesson is B1; taught at A1 here.

title: Come in!: siga, siga, or pase, pase
note: Colombian welcome (siga = come in / go ahead); doubling = warmth, not an order. Tú: pasa, pasa. Peninsular venga/anda dropped. Source lesson is B1; taught at A1 here.

title: How long does it take?: ¿cuánto se demora?

forms.es: ¿Cuánto se demora el bus hasta el centro?
forms.en: How long does the bus take to get to the centre?

note: Colombian; neutral ¿cuánto tarda?

title: Besides, what's more: además
es: El apartamento es barato y, además, queda cerca.
en: The flat is cheap and, what's more, it's close by.
note: Source lesson is A2; taught at A1 here.

title: I mean: o sea

forms.es: Llega el martes, o sea, pasado mañana.
forms.en: She arrives on Tuesday, I mean, the day after tomorrow.

note: Very frequent in Colombian speech; in writing prefer es decir.

title: For example: por ejemplo
es: Me gusta la comida típica, por ejemplo el ajiaco.
en: I like traditional food, for example ajiaco.
note: Narrows a general claim to one case.

title: Well…: pues
note: Opens an answer. Paisa pues at the end of a sentence (¡Hágale pues!): recognition.

title: Dear…: querida Vale
note: Agrees with the person you write TO. Hola, ¿qué tal? is speech, not a first line on paper.

title: Guess what, or Just so you know: te cuento que
es: Te cuento que me cambié de trabajo.

forms.es: Te cuento que me cambié de trabajo.
Les cuento que nos vamos a casar.
forms.en: Just so you all know, we're getting married.

note: Very Colombian opener, spoken and in messages.

title: Signing off: un abrazo, saludos
note: Besos is fine between friends of any sex in LatAm.

title: It depends: depende

forms.en: Yes, but it depends on the day.

note: Expanded later in p:depende-de.

title: I agree: estoy de acuerdo
note: *Estoy acuerdo / *soy de acuerdo.

title: Is something wrong?: ¿te pasa algo?
note: ¿Estás bien? suggests you noticed something; it isn't a general greeting.

title: I feel ill, or better: me siento mal
Not at all: para nada
en:
Does it bother you?
Not at all.

forms.en:
Does it bother you?
Not at all.

title: What a fright! How annoying!: ¡qué susto!, ¡qué rabia!
note: Rabia = annoyance / anger in Colombia. ¡Qué + noun! takes no article (*¡qué una suerte!).

title: Don't worry, it's fine: tranquilo
en: Don't worry, it's fine. (to a man)

forms.en: Don't worry, it's fine. (to a man)
Relax, it's no problem. (to a woman)

note: Huge in Colombia as a reply to apologies; agrees with the listener.

title: How can I help you? (shop): ¿en qué le puedo servir?

forms.en: Can I help you with anything?

note: Colaborar = help, very Colombian service register; recognise it first. Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: I'll take it: me lo llevo
note: Pronoun agrees with the item.

title: Just looking: solo estoy mirando
How many instalments?: ¿a cuántas cuotas?
note: Colombian card terminals ask this for credit cards; recognition. Answer a una.

title: Can I try it on?: ¿me lo puedo medir?

forms.en: Can I try it on? (a feminine noun)

note: Colombian medirse = try on (neutral probarse); vestier = fitting room (Colombia), probador elsewhere.

title: Take care (goodbye): que esté bien
note: Colombian closing in shops and on the phone; learn whole. A bit of small talk (the weather) often comes before it.

title: Card or cash?: ¿tarjeta o efectivo?

forms.en:
Cash or card?
By card, debit.

title: Do you have it in another size?: ¿lo tiene en otra talla?
en: Do you have it in another size?

forms.en: Do you have it in another size?
Do you have it in black?

title: I'd love to: me encantaría

forms.en: I'd love to, but I can't.

note: A warm yes; a bare sí can sound curt.

title: Sounds good: me parece bien
note: Agrees to a proposal; it doesn't judge quality. Peninsular vale → listo / de acuerdo.

title: Maybe another time: será otro día
Let's set it up: ¿cuadramos?
en: Shall we arrange something for Saturday?

forms.en: Shall we arrange something for Saturday?

note: Colombian colloquial cuadrar = arrange; story dialogue / recognition. Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: OK, go for it: ¡dale!
en:
Shall we meet at eight?
Sure!
note: Widespread in LatAm, including Colombia; informal.

title: Let me know: me avisas

forms.en: Let me know when you get there.

note: Avísame = command + pronoun; cuando llegues is a subjunctive learned whole (g:subj-cuando-future). Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: What's the plan?: ¿qué plan?
note: Colombian plan = an outing; recognition of the colloquial ¿qué hay de plan?

title: In the name of…: a nombre de
es: Tengo una reserva a nombre de Matthew.
en: I have a booking in Matthew's name.

forms.es: Tengo una reserva a nombre de Matthew.
forms.en: I have a booking in Matthew's name.

title: Have a good trip: ¡buen viaje!
note: Saying nothing as someone leaves on a trip leaves a gap a Spanish speaker would fill.

title: One way or return?: ¿ida y vuelta?

forms.es: Un pasaje de ida y vuelta a Medellín.

note: pasaje / tiquete (Colombia) / boleto. Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: Can I help you with that?: ¿le ayudo?
en: Can I help you with your suitcase? (formal)

forms.en: Can I help you with your suitcase? (formal)
Shall I help you? (to a friend)

note: Short is normal, not abrupt. Offer unprompted with heavy bags. ¿Necesitas ayuda? asks first and is less presumptuous.

title: Do you want me to help?: ¿quieres que te ayude?
en: Do you want me to help you?

forms.en: Do you want me to help you?
Would you like me to get you a taxi? (formal)

note: Learn whole; the form after que is the subjunctive.

title: I'm here (safely): ya llegué

forms.en: We got here safely, thank God.

note: The message family expects. Preterite in LatAm (not *he llegado). Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: Hello? (phone): ¿aló?
note: Colombian / LatAm. Spain's ¿Dígame? is recognition only.

title: Speaking: sí, con ella
note: Colombian phone formula for 'speaking'; neutral alternative Sí, soy yo. Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: Who's calling?: ¿de parte de quién?

forms.es:
¿De parte de quién?
De parte de Matthew.

note: A bare ¿Quién es? / ¿Quién eres? is blunt on the phone.

title: Can I take a message?: ¿quiere dejarle un mensaje?
en: Would you like to leave her a message?

forms.en: Would you like to leave her a message?
Shall I pass on a message?

forms.es: En este momento no puede pasar.
forms.en: She can't come to the phone right now.

note: Dejar razón = leave a message (Colombian). Spain's recado → mensaje.

title: Hiring: se necesita, se busca
note: Job ads and signs; scan for the one fact you need.

title: May I come in?: ¿se puede?

forms.en: Is it OK to come in?

note: Asks without saying yo, so it sounds less exposed. Answer: Siga. Hay que + infinitive does the same for rules (Hay que llevar corbata).

title: Just a moment: un momentico
note: -ico after t: momentico, ratico (Colombian).

title: Maybe: a lo mejor
note: A lo mejor takes the ordinary (indicative) form.

title: Could be: puede ser
en:
It's going to rain.
Could be.

forms.en:
It's going to rain.
Could be.

note: Puede ser is the most hedged; es probable is close to agreeing.

title: I suppose so: supongo que sí

forms.es: Supongo que está en la oficina.
forms.en: I suppose she's at the office.

title: Maybe (Colombian): de pronto
en: It might rain, take an umbrella.

forms.en: It might rain, take an umbrella.
Maybe we'll see each other there.

note: Colombian de pronto = maybe (elsewhere it means suddenly). Use it with Colombians; recognise it everywhere.

title: The best thing is to…: lo mejor es…
en: The best thing is to leave early.

forms.en: The best thing is to leave early.
The best thing is to rest.

title: I promise: te lo prometo
Everything will be OK: todo va a salir bien
es: Tranquilo, todo va a salir bien. Todo saldrá bien.
en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
note: Reassurance formula; va a salir is more conversational, saldrá more solemn. Source lesson is B1; taught at A2 here.

title: If I were you…: yo que tú…
es: Yo que tú, iría en bus.
en: If I were you, I'd go by bus.

forms.es: Yo que tú, iría en bus.
forms.en: If I were you, I'd go by bus.

forms.es: Yo en tu lugar, no compraría eso.
forms.en: In your shoes, I wouldn't buy that.

note: Softer than tienes que; hay que / es necesario advise without pointing at anyone.

title: Can you do me a favour?: ¿me haces un favor?
en: Can you do me a favour?

forms.en: Can you do me a favour?
Can you do me a favour? (formal)
Can I ask you a favour?

note: Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: Don't worry: no te preocupes
note: Negative command learned whole (te / se before the verb).

title: No problem: sin problema
note: An unreserved yes.

title: Well, I don't know…: bueno, no sé…
es:
¿Me ayudas a trastear el sábado?
Bueno, no sé.
en:
Can you help me move house on Saturday?
Well, I don't know.
note: Evasive: neither yes nor no. Bueno, listo said slowly = a reluctant yes. Trastear = to move house (Colombian).

title: Please would you…: hágame el favor
es: Hágame el favor y me espera.

forms.es: Hágame el favor y me espera.
Hágame el favor de cerrar la puerta.
Hazme un favor: llama a Vale.
forms.en: Do me a favour: call Vale.

note: Polite in Colombia, but can turn firm with tone.

title: Sorry to bother you, but…: qué pena molestarlo
es: Qué pena molestarlo, pero ¿sabe dónde queda el banco?
en: Sorry to bother you, but do you know where the bank is? (to a man)

forms.es: Qué pena molestarlo, pero ¿sabe dónde queda el banco?
forms.en: Sorry to bother you, but do you know where the bank is? (to a man)

forms.es: Qué pena con usted, ¿me podría ayudar con la maleta?
forms.en: I'm so sorry, could you help me with my suitcase? (formal)

note: Very Colombian polite opener; qué pena con usted = I'm so sorry / excuse me.

title: Happy birthday: ¡feliz cumpleaños!
Have fun: ¡que la pases bien!
note: LatAm la (Spain lo pases bien).

title: All the best: ¡que te vaya bien!
Season's greetings: ¡feliz Navidad!
I'm so glad: me alegro mucho
note: Me alegro de que hayas venido can be taken whole until the subjunctive arrives.

title: Good luck!: ¡mucha suerte!
note: ¡Éxitos! is very common in Colombia.

title: My condolences: mi sentido pésame

forms.en: I'm here for you at this time.

title: Have a good day: ¡que tengas un buen día!
note: ¡Feliz día! is a common close in Colombia.

title: It doesn't work: no funciona, no sirve
note: LatAm no sirve = broken; se dañó (Colombia) = it broke.

title: What do I need to do?: ¿qué tengo que hacer?
en: What do I have to do?

forms.en: What do I have to do?
Where do I have to sign?

title: I wanted to ask…: quería…
en: I wanted to ask about my order.

forms.en: I wanted to ask about my order.

forms.es: Quería cambiar esto, es que no funciona.
forms.en: I wanted to exchange this; it's just that it doesn't work.

note: Imperfect as politeness, softer than quiero. Source lesson is A1; taught at A2 here.

title: Could you help me with…?: ¿me colabora?
es: ¿Me colabora con el número de cédula?
en: Could you give me your ID number?

forms.es: ¿Me colabora con el número de cédula?
forms.en: Could you give me your ID number?
Could you sign here for me?

note: Colombian service register; recognise it first, use later.

title: I have to / It's my turn: me toca

forms.en: We have to come back tomorrow.

note: Colombian (toca + infinitive) = have to, resigned. Me hace falta works the same way for what's missing.

title: The good thing is…: lo bueno es que…
es: Lo bueno es que queda cerca.
en: The good thing is it's close by.

forms.es: Lo bueno es que queda cerca.
forms.en: The good thing is it's close by.

forms.es: Lo malo es que es caro.
forms.en: The bad thing is it's expensive.

title: I'm not convinced: no me convence
On the one hand… on the other: por un lado… por otro
es: Por un lado, es más barato; por otro, queda lejos.
en: On the one hand, it's cheaper; on the other, it's far away.

forms.es: Por un lado, es más barato; por otro, queda lejos.
forms.en: On the one hand, it's cheaper; on the other, it's far away.

forms.es: Por un lado, es más barato; por otro lado, queda lejos.
forms.en: On the one hand, it's cheaper; on the other hand, it's far away.

title: The plan is to…: la idea es…
es: La idea es mudarnos en enero.
en: The idea is to move in January.

forms.es: La idea es mudarnos en enero.
forms.en: The idea is to move in January.
The idea is to save money.

note: Very common LatAm way to state a goal.

title: Not at all!: ¡qué va!
en:
Are you tired?
Not at all!

forms.en:
Are you tired?
Not at all!

note: Friendly contradiction, understood everywhere; Colombians also say ¡Nada que ver! (no way / beside the point).

title: Anyway, still: igual
es: Es caro, pero igual lo voy a tomar.
en: It's expensive, but I'm going to take it anyway.

forms.es: Es caro, pero igual lo voy a tomar.
forms.en: It's expensive, but I'm going to take it anyway.

note: Colombian igual = anyway / still; recognition first.

title: The weather's lovely there: tiene buen clima
note: Colombian clima = typical weather / temperature; tierra caliente / fría = hot lowlands / cold highlands.

title: A really kind person: es un pan de Dios
According to…: según
es: Según Vale, el clima allá es delicioso.
en: According to Vale, the weather there is lovely.

forms.es: Según Vale, el clima allá es delicioso.
forms.en: According to Vale, the weather there is lovely.

forms.es: Según el pronóstico, va a llover.
forms.en: According to the forecast, it's going to rain.

title: Supposedly: dizque
es: Dizque va a llover toda la semana.
en: Supposedly it's going to rain all week.
note: Colombian / LatAm hearsay marker, colloquial: recognition only.

title: It's an hour away: queda a una hora
es: Queda a una hora de Medellín.

forms.es: Queda a una hora de Medellín.

note: Spanish measures short distances in minutes more than metres.

title: She told me that…: me contó que
es: Me contó que se iba a vivir a Medellín.
en: She told me she was moving to Medellín.

forms.es: Me contó que se iba a vivir a Medellín.
forms.en: She told me she was moving to Medellín.
He told me he was tired.

note: Contar = tell (news); preguntar reports questions (me preguntó si…).

title: No way!: ¡no me digas!
note: For big news only. ¡Mentiras! = no way! (Colombian, playful). Spain's ¡qué fuerte! is not used.

title: It turns out that…: resulta que
es: Resulta que el bus nunca llegó.
en: It turns out the bus never came.

forms.es: Resulta que el bus nunca llegó.
forms.en: It turns out the bus never came.

forms.es: Y resulta que era su hermana.
forms.en: And it turned out she was his sister.

title: Guess what happened to me?: ¿sabes qué me pasó?

forms.es:
¿Te cuento una cosa?
Sí, claro, cuéntame.
forms.en:
Can I tell you something?
Yes, of course, tell me.

note: Turning someone away needs apology + reason: Qué pena, es que tengo afán.

title: Imagine!: ¡imagínate!
What bad luck!: ¡qué de malas!
note: Qué de malas is Colombian; de buenas = lucky.

title: How embarrassing!: ¡qué oso!
note: Colombian / Mexican colloquial: story dialogue / recognition. Hacer el oso = embarrass yourself.

title: So anyway…: total, que…
es: Total, que llegamos a las tres de la mañana.
en: So anyway, we got there at three in the morning.
note: Wraps up the complication and moves to the outcome.

title: Email opening: cordial saludo
note: Colombian business emails often OPEN with Cordial saludo; Un cordial saludo closes. Estimado/a + title takes a colon.

title: Thanks in advance: gracias de antemano

forms.en: Thank you very much for your attention.

title: I look forward to hearing from you: quedo atento
en: I look forward to your reply. (a man writing)

forms.en: I look forward to your reply. (a man writing)
I look forward to hearing from you. (a woman writing)
We look forward to hearing from you.

note: Agrees with the writer; standard Colombian email close.

title: Please find attached: adjunto le envío
en: I'm sending you the document attached.

forms.en: I'm sending you the document attached.

title: Yours sincerely: atentamente
note: Match the opening: usted throughout.

title: I recommend it: lo recomiendo
note: Reviews.

title: So glad that…: ¡qué bueno que…!
note: With something not yet real, the subjunctive: qué bueno que vengas.

title: With a bit of luck: Con un poco de suerte
es: Con un poco de suerte, llegamos antes de la lluvia.
en: With a bit of luck we'll get there before the rain.
note: Also A ver si… (let's hope). Source lesson is B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Sleep well, or Rest up: que descanses
note: Reply: Igualmente / Tú también. Source lesson is B1; taught at A2 here.

title: Have fun: que te diviertas, que la pases bien
es: ¡Que la pases bien en la fiesta!
en: Have a good time at the party!

forms.es: ¡Que la pases bien en la fiesta!
forms.en: Have a good time at the party!

note: Que la pases bien is the LatAm favourite. Source lesson is B1; taught at A2 here.

title: No way: ¡Ni hablar!
As far as I know: Que yo sepa
es: Que yo sepa, todavía no han abierto.
en: As far as I know, they haven't opened yet.
note: Learn whole; the subjunctive in a relative-like frame is unpacked later.

title: Doubtful echo: ¿Tú crees?
en:
We're going to win.
You think so?
note: Genuinely sceptical, not a request for confirmation.

title: I can imagine: Me imagino
es:
Estuve en el hospital toda la noche.
Me imagino, qué cansancio.
en:
I was at the hospital all night.
I can imagine, how exhausting.
note: Very frequent LatAm empathy token; also Te entiendo.

title: What a relief!: ¡Qué alivio!
en: What a relief you got there OK!
note: Que llegaste (indicative) is common in LatAm exclamations of relief; que hayas llegado is also fine.

title: How annoying!: ¡Qué rabia!
es: ¡Qué rabia! Perdí el bus otra vez.
en: How annoying! I missed the bus again.

title: Getting by: Ahí vamos
en:
How's everything going?
Getting by, and you?
note: LatAm 'so-so' reply; always bounce the question back. Replaces Peninsular aquí andamos.

title: Chin up, you can do it: ¡Ánimo! ¡Tú puedes!
en: Come on, you can do it!

title: It's not that bad: No es para tanto
en: Relax, it's not that big a deal.
note: Can sound dismissive if the other person is genuinely hurt.

title: You'll see, it'll all work out: Ya verás que todo sale bien
es: No te preocupes, ya verás que todo sale bien.
en: Don't worry, you'll see it'll all work out.

title: You won't believe it: No te lo vas a creer
es: ¿Sabes qué pasó? No te lo vas a creer.
en: You know what happened? You won't believe it.
note: Rhetorical: buys the floor; no answer expected.

title: Sorry, I can't: Lo siento, pero no puedo
es: Lo siento, pero no puedo. Es que tengo turno.
en: Sorry, I can't. I'm on shift.
note: Needs the es que reason after it.

title: Can you give me a hand?: ¿Me echas una mano?
es: ¿Me echas una mano con la mudanza?
en: Can you give me a hand with the move?
note: Also ¿me das una mano? / ¿me ayudas con…? across LatAm.

title: I need to ask you a favour: Tengo que pedirte un favor
es: Tengo que pedirte un favor: ¿podrías cuidarme el perro este fin de semana?
en: I need to ask you a favour: could you look after my dog this weekend?
note: Announces a big or awkward ask; heavy for something trivial.

title: Hurry up: ¡apúrate!
es: ¡Apúrate, que vamos tarde! Estoy de afán. No hay afán.
en: Hurry up, we're late! I'm in a rush. There's no rush.
note: Replaces Spain's date prisa. Afán is Colombian; tener prisa understood everywhere.

title: Well, if you insist: Bueno, si insistes…
es:
Quédate a comer.
Bueno, si insistes.
en:
Stay for lunch.
Well, if you insist.
note: Signals reluctant acceptance — wrong signal for something you want.

title: Another time: Otra vez será
I didn't mean to: No fue mi intención
es: Perdón, no fue mi intención ofenderte.
en: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
note: LatAm preterite; Peninsular no era mi intención also fine.

title: It's nothing: No tiene importancia
note: Accepting an apology works by minimising the issue; no 'apology accepted' formula. Also No pasa nada, Olvídalo.

title: These things happen: Son cosas que pasan
es: No te preocupes, son cosas que pasan.

title: Luckily: por suerte
es: Por suerte no le pasó nada. ¡Qué suerte!
en: Luckily nothing happened to him. What luck!
note: Also menos mal (que…) — very common in Colombia.

title: Don't forget: Que no se te olvide
es: Que no se te olvide la cédula.
note: Que + subjunctive as an order/warning.

title: Queuing: hacer fila
es: Toca hacer fila para la cita. Había una fila enorme.
en: We have to queue for the appointment. There was a huge queue.
note: LatAm hacer fila (Spain hacer cola). En orden / por orden alfabético. Ordering phrases: por orden alfabético, en primer lugar / puesto, quedar de tercero (Col.).

title: Don't even think about it: Ni se te ocurra
es: Ni se te ocurra abrir esa puerta.
en: Don't even think about opening that door.

title: Well done: ¡Bien hecho!, ¡Buen trabajo!
note: Praise for an achievement; holiday formulas are a separate, fixed family.

title: Do you see what I mean?: ¿Me explico?
es: Es que no es solo el precio, ¿me explico?
en: It's not just the price, do you see what I mean?
note: Also ¿me entiendes?, tag ¿sí? / ¿no?

title: By the way: Por cierto
en: By the way, did you hear about Andrés?

title: And then what?: ¿Y entonces? ¿Y qué pasó?
en: And then? Go on, tell me.
note: Spanish expects a listening token every three or four sentences (claro, ya, ajá, ¿en serio?).

title: That's all, thanks: Listo, eso sería todo
es: Listo, eso sería todo. Muchas gracias, muy amable.
en: Great, that's everything. Thank you very much.
note: Part of the closing ritual: satisfaction → boundary phrase → last chance → goodbye. Skipping straight to adiós sounds abrupt.

title: Can you hear me? (phone): ¿Me escuchas? Se te está cortando
en: Can you hear me? You're breaking up.
note: LatAm uses escuchar for phone hearing; ¿sigues ahí? = are you still there?

title: He's not available: En este momento no se encuentra
es: En este momento no se encuentra. ¿Quiere dejarle algún mensaje?
en: She's not available right now. Would you like to leave a message?
note: Always offer the message; a bare 'no está' is a dead end.

title: Wrong number: Creo que tiene el número equivocado
es: Disculpe, creo que tiene el número equivocado.
en: Sorry, I think you have the wrong number.
note: ≠ no se encuentra (right number, wrong moment).

title: Closing politely: No, así está bien, gracias
es:
¿Algo más?
No, así está bien, gracias.
en:
Anything else?
No, that's fine, thanks.

forms.es:
¿Algo más?
No, así está bien, gracias.
forms.en:
Anything else?
No, that's fine, thanks.

note: Fixed closing that declines more without rejecting. Así está bien.

title: What do you mean?: ¿cómo así?

forms.en: What do you mean, he left?

note: Colombian staple for asking for clarification with surprise; neutral elsewhere: ¿Cómo es eso? / ¿Cómo es que…? Source lesson is C1; taught at B1 here.

title: Guess what, or You know what: fíjese que
en: You know what, I couldn't make it. (formal)

forms.en: You know what, I couldn't make it. (formal)
Guess what, Juliana got married. (to a friend)

note: Imperative used as a news opener, no command. Common in Colombia and Central America. Related p:fijarse-reparar-en (to notice). Source lesson is B2; taught at B1 here.

title: That rings a bell: me suena

forms.en:
Do you know Andrés?
He doesn't ring a bell.

note: Sonar (gustar pattern). Sonar also: sonó el timbre / el celular (source as subject). Source lesson is B2; taught at B1 here.

title: Thank you for your attention: Muchas gracias por su atención
es: Eso es todo. Muchas gracias por su atención.
en: That's all. Thank you for your attention.

title: Did you know…? (to an audience): ¿Sabían que…?
es: ¿Sabían que Bogotá tiene más de 500 kilómetros de ciclorrutas?
en: Did you know that Bogotá has more than 500 kilometres of cycle lanes? (you all)
note: Ustedes, never ¿sabíais…? (vosotros).

title: Count on me: cuenta conmigo
es: Si necesitas algo, cuenta conmigo. Cuento contigo.
en: If you need anything, count on me.
note: Seeds contar con (rely on).

title: It's not fair: No hay derecho
es: No hay derecho a que nos traten así.
en: It's not right that they treat us like this.

title: Whenever you like: cuando quieras
note: Register: coloquial-neutral. Fixed subjunctive; unpacked by subj-free-relatives.

title: Door signs: Empuje and Hale

forms.en: To open it, you have to pull.

note: Colombia: halar / jalar for pull (Spain tirar — recognition). Classic sign mix-up.

title: Ordering delivery: ¿pedimos un domicilio?
es: ¿Pedimos un domicilio? El domicilio cuesta tres mil.
en: Shall we order delivery? Delivery costs three thousand.
note: Colombian domicilio = home delivery. Story dialogue / everyday.

title: Overwhelming thanks: no sé cómo agradecértelo
es: No sé cómo agradecértelo, de verdad.
en: I don't know how to thank you.
note: Register: neutral, hyperbolic — too much for small favours. Usted: no sé cómo agradecérselo.

title: This once: que sea la última vez
es: Bueno, pero que sea la última vez.
en: OK, but this is the last time.
note: Register: coloquial-neutral; permission with a reproach, or a closing threat.

title: Reluctant yes: bueno, si no hay más remedio
es: Bueno, si no hay más remedio.
en: Well, if there's no other way.

forms.es: Bueno, si no hay más remedio.
forms.en: Well, if there's no other way.

note: Register: coloquial. Yes, visibly unwanted.

title: We'll see: ya veremos
en:
Will you buy me one?
Well, we'll see.
note: Register: coloquial. A real non-answer — neither yes nor no.

title: Fingers crossed: crucemos los dedos
es: Crucemos los dedos para que salga bien.
note: Register: coloquial-neutral. Illness-specific wishes (que te mejores, que te recuperes pronto) don't transfer to other occasions.

title: Formal good wishes: le deseo lo mejor
es: Le deseo lo mejor en esta nueva etapa.
en: I wish you all the best.
note: Register: neutral-formal; works for almost any occasion.

title: To be honest: para serte sincero
es: Para serte sincero, no me gustó.
en: To be honest, I didn't like it.

forms.es: Para serte sincero, no me gustó.
forms.en: To be honest, I didn't like it.

forms.es: Para serte sincera, no me gustó.
forms.en: To be honest, I didn't like it. (said by a woman)

forms.es: Para ser sinceros, no nos gustó.
forms.en: To be honest, we didn't like it.
Just so you know, I've already paid.

note: Parenthetical purpose clauses used as softeners/discourse markers. Usted: para serle sincero. Source lesson is C1; taught at B2 here.

title: Please hold: permítame un momento
es: Permítame un momento, no cuelgue, por favor.
note: Register: formal phone/service. Converted from Peninsular 'no se retire'. Colombian: un momentico.

title: Oh well, nothing to be done: ni modo
es: Se canceló el vuelo. Ni modo, nos toca esperar.
en: The flight was cancelled. Oh well, we'll have to wait.
note: Register: coloquial; Colombian/Mexican everyday resignation. Replaces Peninsular shrugs.

title: Not bad at all: no está nada mal
es: No está nada mal para ser la primera vez.
en: Not bad at all for a first try.
note: Understated praise.

title: What can you do: ¿qué le vamos a hacer?
es: Perdimos el bus. ¿Qué le vamos a hacer?
note: Register: coloquial. Mild, almost cheerful — flippant for serious losses. Also 'otra vez será' (maybe next time).

title: Hoping, as a reply: eso espero
es:
¿Crees que lleguemos a tiempo?
Eso espero.
en:
Do you think we'll get there in time?
I hope so.
note: Register: neutral. Only as a reply. Negative: eso espero que no / ojalá que no.

title: Promising effort: voy a hacer todo lo posible
es: Voy a hacer todo lo posible por conseguir las boletas.
en: I'm going to do everything I can to get the tickets.
note: Register: neutral. Commits to effort, not success. LatAm boletas (Colombia) / entradas.

title: It's hopeless: no hay nada que hacer
es: Esto no tiene arreglo; no hay nada que hacer.
en: This can't be fixed; there's nothing to be done.
note: Register: neutral; flat closure. Formal: la situación no tiene solución a corto plazo.

title: In the short and long term: a corto plazo, a largo plazo
es: A corto plazo no hay solución, pero a largo plazo sí. Es una inversión a largo plazo.
en: In the short term there's no solution, but in the long term there is.
note: LatAm a mediano plazo (Spain medio plazo). Classifies timing, not importance.

title: The root of the problem: la raíz del problema
es: Hay que atacar la raíz del problema, no los síntomas.
en: We need to tackle the root of the problem, not the symptoms.
note: Fixed metaphor; do not extend raíz to every 'origin'.

title: I'm absolutely sure: lo tengo clarísimo
es: Lo tengo clarísimo: no voy a cambiar de opinión.
note: Tenerlo (muy) claro = be sure, not about eyesight.

title: Unreserved agreement: desde luego
note: Register: neutral. Also 'claro que sí', '¡por supuesto!'.

title: Casual agreement: pues sí
note: Register: coloquial — the bottom rung of the agreement ladder.

title: No doubt about it: sin duda alguna
es: Sin duda alguna, es la mejor opción.
note: Register: neutral-formal; spoken and written. No me cabe (ninguna) duda is the personal version.

title: Polite disagreement: yo no lo veo así
en: I don't see it that way.

forms.en: I don't see it that way.

forms.es: Yo no lo veo tan claro.
forms.en: I don't see it as that clear.

note: Register: neutral. Softer than 'no estoy de acuerdo'.

title: Admitting you might be wrong first: puede que me equivoque, pero…
es: Puede que me equivoque, pero yo lo veo de otra manera.
en: I may be wrong, but I see it differently.
note: Register: neutral. Dialogic softening before disagreement; also 'es posible que esté equivocado'.

title: Polite scepticism: si tú lo dices
es:
Juan está estudiando muchísimo.
Si tú lo dices.
en:
Juan is studying really hard.
If you say so.
note: Register: coloquial. Not agreement — hands the claim back. A bare skeptical 'Ya.' does the same, with a deflating follow-up.

title: Who knows: quién sabe
en:
Will he come back?
Who knows.
note: Register: coloquial. Converted from Peninsular 'A saber' (recognition).

title: Before I forget: antes de que se me olvide
es: Antes de que se me olvide: el viernes no hay clase.
en: Before I forget: there's no class on Friday.
note: Register: coloquial-neutral; justifies interrupting.

title: Holding the floor: déjame terminar
note: Register: neutral. Usted: déjeme terminar. Blunter: Estoy hablando yo.

title: Lost the thread: ¿en qué íbamos?
es: ¿En qué íbamos? Se me fue la idea.
en: Where were we? I lost my train of thought.
note: Register: coloquial. Also ¿De qué estábamos hablando?

title: Refusing a topic: mejor no hablemos de eso
en: Let's not talk about that, OK?
note: Register: coloquial-neutral (Peninsular '¿vale?' → '¿listo?'). Formal writing: Preferimos no hacer comentarios al respecto.

title: Checking they've got time: ¿tienes un minutico?
es: ¿Tienes un minutico? Es que quería contarte una cosa.
note: Register: coloquial, very Colombian diminutive.

title: Over and over: una y otra vez
es: Lo intentamos una y otra vez hasta que funcionó.
en: We tried over and over until it worked.
note: Also una vez más, de nuevo (nuevamente = more formal).

title: Following along: ya me imagino
es:
Y claro, Carlos no hizo nada.
Sí, ya me imagino.
en:
And of course, Carlos didn't do anything.
Yes, I can imagine.
note: Register: coloquial. Claims you can picture it; 'Normal' validates it as unsurprising; ¡No me digas! keeps them going.

title: Missing someone: me haces mucha falta
es: Te extraño. Me haces mucha falta.
en: I miss you. I really miss you.
note: Register: neutral, affectionate. Converted from Peninsular 'te echo de menos' (recognition u51). Calmer, deeper: me importas.

title: Frozen with surprise: me quedé de piedra
es: Me quedé de piedra cuando me dieron la noticia.
note: Register: coloquial, fixed. Blushing: ponerse rojo como un tomate.

title: Flat defiance: no me da la gana
es: No pienso ir. No me da la gana.
en: I'm not going. I just don't feel like it.
note: Register: coloquial and rude — much stronger than no quiero. Never at work.

title: At breaking point: ¡no puedo más!
note: Register: coloquial.

title: Half-accepting an apology: está bien, pero que no se repita
es: Está bien, pero que no se vuelva a repetir.
en: OK, but don't let it happen again.
note: Register: neutral. Forgiveness plus a warning. Full acceptance: No pasa nada / Tranquilo.

title: Keep going: ¡ánimo, que ya falta poco!
note: Register: coloquial. LatAm 'falta poco' (Spain 'queda poco').

title: Showing you understand: te entiendo perfectamente
note: Register: neutral. Claims understanding, not the same experience.

title: Reassurance: todo tiene solución
en: There's a way out of everything.
note: Register: neutral, proverbial.

title: It's over now: ya pasó
note: Register: coloquial. LatAm preterite (Spain ya ha pasado). Only for a finished crisis; for an ongoing one: todo se va a arreglar.

title: Same here: a mí me pasa lo mismo
es: A mí me pasa lo mismo, no te preocupes.
note: Register: coloquial. Claims shared experience — hollow if untrue.

title: Hablando se entiende la gente: let's talk it through
en: People understand each other by talking.
note: Gerund as a condition ("if you talk…"). Useful opener for a hard conversation. Source lesson is C1; taught at B2 here.

title: Spain's ¡anda!, meaning ¡uy! or ¡no me digas!
en: Oh! You've got the same name as my dad!
note: Recognition only; surprise, nothing to do with walking.

title: Spain's '¡qué rollo!' = ¡qué pereza!
note: Recognition only. Also Spain 'lo pasé fatal / me lo pasé genial' = la pasé muy mal / delicioso.

title: Spain's vale, meaning listo or de acuerdo
es:
Nos vemos a las ocho.
Vale.
note: Recognition only. Never in our es fields; say listo, de acuerdo, bueno.

title: Spain's 'echar de menos' = extrañar
note: Recognition only; LatAm extrañar. Also Spain 'me hace ilusión' ≈ me emociona.

title: In minute detail: con pelos y señales
es: contar algo con pelos y señales
en: to tell something in minute detail
note: Natural across Latin America.

title: Overnight: de la noche a la mañana
es: de la noche a la mañana
note: Se transformó de la noche a la mañana. Figurative: sudden change, not literally overnight.

title: Never in my life: nunca en mi vida
es: Nunca en mi vida había visto algo así.
en: Never in my life had I seen anything like it.
note: Usually with the pluperfect in stories.

title: By a hair: por un pelo

forms.en: He escaped by the skin of his teeth.

note: Replaces Peninsular 'por los pelos' (recognisable but LatAm says 'por un pelo'). Means just in time, NOT late.

title: That was quite an ordeal: ¡fue toda una odisea!
note: Typical for travel and paperwork stories: Conseguir la visa fue toda una odisea.

title: Let's get to work: ¡manos a la obra!

forms.es: Nos pusimos manos a la obra.

note: Pan-Hispanic. Colombian speakers often add or substitute '¡De una!'.

title: ¡Y yo qué sabía!
en: How was I supposed to know!
note: Imperfecto de excusa — a defence, not a report.

title: Dicho sea de paso
es: Y dicho sea de paso, nadie me avisó.
note: Parenthetical aside, often slipping in a pointed remark. Not in the source lessons; added per brief.

title: Whereabouts unknown: en paradero desconocido
es: El sospechoso se encuentra en paradero desconocido.
note: Fixed news/police formula; never conversational.

title: Bueno, no creas, or tanto como eso, no
es:
Debe estar destapada la carretera.
Bueno, no creas, está bastante bien.
en:
The road must be a dirt track by now.
Well, not really, it's in pretty good shape.

forms.es:
Debe estar destapada la carretera.
Bueno, no creas, está bastante bien.
forms.en:
The road must be a dirt track by now.
Well, not really, it's in pretty good shape.

forms.es:
Debe estar destapada la carretera.
Tanto como eso, no.
forms.en:
The road must be a dirt track by now.
I wouldn't go that far.

note: Shrinks the other's claim instead of contradicting it. 'No es para tanto' is the same move.

title: No es por nada, pero…
es: No es por nada, pero ese color no te queda.
en: Don't take this the wrong way, but that colour doesn't suit you.
note: Casual pre-criticism disclaimer; the formal cousin is 'sin ánimo de ofender'.

title: Unprecedented: sin precedentes
note: Strong: nothing comparable has ever happened. Not a synonym of 'nuevo'.

title: Así es, or efectivamente
es:
¿Ya lo sabe?
Así es, se lo dijeron ayer.
en:
Does he know already?
That's right, they told him yesterday.
note: Formal confirmation; casual '¡Claro que sí!'. Spain's '¡Y tanto!' dropped (Peninsular).

title: De ser así: if that's the case
es: De ser así, tendríamos que repetir la votación.
en: If so, we'd have to repeat the vote.

forms.es: De ser así, tendríamos que repetir la votación.
forms.en: If so, we'd have to repeat the vote.

forms.es: De no ser así, seguimos con el plan.
forms.en: If not, we carry on with the plan.

note: Formal conditional with de + infinitive; unpacked by g:conditional-advanced (u57: de haberlo sabido). Frame: De ser así, … / De no ser así, …

title: Lo tengo en la punta de la lengua.
es: ¿Cómo se llamaba ese actor? Lo tengo en la punta de la lengua.
en: It's on the tip of my tongue.
note: You know it but can't retrieve it. Also 'Me quedé en blanco' (went blank), 'No me dice nada' (rings no bell).

title: Conspicuous by its absence: brilla por su ausencia
es: La organización brilló por su ausencia.
en: Organisation was conspicuous by its absence.
note: Ironic: used for something that should be there and isn't.

title: Hardly anyone: había cuatro gatos
es: Había cuatro gatos en la fiesta.
en: There was hardly anyone at the party.
note: Understood across LatAm. Not literal.

title: On and on about the same thing: ¡y dale con lo mismo!

forms.es: Y él, dale que dale con el tema.
forms.en: And he just kept going on and on about it.

note: Replaces Peninsular 'erre que erre' (dropped). '¡Y dale!' is very common in Colombia and across LatAm for annoying insistence.

title: Not a soul: no había ni un alma
es: A esa hora no había ni un alma en la calle.
en: There wasn't a soul in the street.
note: Pan-Hispanic. Opposite end: 'estaba lleno a reventar'.

title: Ironic 'for a change': para variar
en: He was late, for a change.
note: Ironic use is the C1 point: it marks that the annoying thing is routine. Literal use also exists (vamos a otro sitio, para variar).

title: Talking non-stop: habla por los codos
note: Pan-Hispanic.

title: Not mincing words: no tiene pelos en la lengua
es: No tiene pelos en la lengua.
note: Pan-Hispanic; usually admiring or warning.

title: You haven't aged a bit: ¡por ti no pasan los años!
note: Always a compliment; can be teasing.

title: Costing an arm and a leg: cuesta un ojo de la cara
es: Ese carro le costó un ojo de la cara.
en: That car cost him an arm and a leg.
note: Pan-Hispanic. Colombian: 'costó un platal'. Replaces Peninsular 'una millonada' (use 'un dineral').

title: Out of line: fuera de lugar
es: Ese comentario estuvo fuera de lugar.
en: That comment was out of line.
note: Pan-Hispanic; the everyday version of 'improcedente'.

title: What an outrage: ¡qué barbaridad!
note: Indignation; in some regions also 'a huge amount' (una barbaridad de gente).

title: Double meaning: tiene doble sentido
note: Colombian humour leans heavily on 'doble sentido'; links to mamar gallo in the unit.

title: Mamar gallo or tomar el pelo
note: 'Tomar el pelo' is general; 'mamar gallo' is Colombian banter — story dialogue/recognition (unit 54 theme). Frozen metaphors for vocab: costar un ojo de la cara, llover a cántaros, tener los pies en la tierra.

title: ¡Ni amarrado!
en: Not a chance! (not even if you tied me up)
note: LatAm equivalent of Spain's '¡Ni atado!'. Top of the ni-scale.

title: No se queda atrás: doesn't lag behind
es: Y ella no se queda atrás.

forms.es: Y ella no se queda atrás.
Su hermano tampoco se queda atrás.
forms.en: Her brother is no slouch either.

note: tampoco here doesn't negate; it equates (Si él habla mucho, ella tampoco se queda atrás). Often ironic.

title: …, que ya es algo.
es: Al menos llegó, que ya es algo.
en: At least he came, which is something.
note: Tag that salvages one positive. Frame: Al menos / Por lo menos + clause, que ya es algo — exclusive focus; also comforts.

title: Eso vale su platica.
es: Me gusta, pero vale su platica.
note: Colombian: the diminutive here intensifies, not reduces (cf. Spain 'un dinerillo'). Regional — recognition/story dialogue.

title: At cost: a precio de costo
es: Vendemos el café a precio de costo.
en: We sell the coffee at cost.
note: LatAm conversion: 'costo' (Spain 'coste'). 'Precio de fábrica' also fine.

title: Sin otro particular…
es: Sin otro particular, me despido atentamente.
en: With nothing further to add, I remain yours sincerely.
note: Written only. In Colombian correspondence the usual close is 'Cordialmente,'.

title: Without a doubt: sin lugar a dudas
es: Sin lugar a dudas, es su mejor novela.
en: Without a shadow of a doubt, it's her best novel.
note: Strongest booster — disproportionate for a merely probable claim.

title: Sooner or later: tarde o temprano
es: Tarde o temprano se sabrá la verdad.
en: Sooner or later the truth will come out.

title: Sleeping on it: consultarlo con la almohada
note: Pan-Hispanic; postponing a decision, not insomnia.

title: You've got nothing to lose: el no ya lo tienes
es: Pregúntale. El no ya lo tienes.
en: Ask her. The worst she can say is no.
note: 'El sí / el no' as nouns: dar el sí, recibir un no.

title: An everyday thing (sadly): es el pan de cada día
es: Los trancones son el pan de cada día.
en: Traffic jams are an everyday thing here.
note: Usually resigned/negative. 'Trancón' = Colombian traffic jam.

title: That's where I draw the line: ¡eso sí que no!
note: Replaces Peninsular 'no paso por eso'. Firm personal limit.

title: Keeping up appearances: guardar las formas
es: Supo guardar las formas aunque estaba furiosa.
en: She managed to keep up appearances even though she was furious.
note: Doesn't mean agreeing: social composure despite inner disagreement.

title: Mi más sentido pésame.
es: Quisiera expresarle mi más sentido pésame.
note: Ritual; also 'Te acompaño en el sentimiento' and warmer 'Estoy contigo'.

title: ¡Qué embarrada!
note: Colombian disappointment — replaces Spain's '¡Vaya, hombre!'. General: '¡Qué lástima! / ¡Qué decepción!'. Story dialogue/recognition.

title: Que sea lo que Dios quiera.
es: Ya hice todo lo que pude; que sea lo que Dios quiera.
en: I've done all I could; whatever will be, will be.
note: Fatalistic formula, not necessarily religious.

title: Cruzo los dedos, or toco madera
es: Cruzo los dedos para que todo salga bien mañana.
en: I'm keeping my fingers crossed that everything goes well tomorrow.
note: Protects a fragile hope. 'La esperanza es lo último que se pierde.'

title: Estoy molido, or estoy muerto
en: I'm wiped out after the move.
note: For Spain's 'estoy hecho polvo / no puedo con mi alma'. 'Trasteo' = house move (Colombia). Also 'Se me cierran los ojos'.

title: ¡Dale! or ¡Hágale!
en: Are you scared? Go for it, you can do it! (formal)
note: Replaces Spain's '¡A por ello!'. '¡Hágale!' is Colombian (story dialogue). Also 'No te dé pena' for Spain's 'no te cortes'.

title: No te lo tomes a pecho.
es: Tranquilo, no te lo tomes a pecho.
note: With 'No es el fin del mundo' for perspective.

title: Como el que más: as much as anyone
en: She works as hard as anyone.

forms.en: She works as hard as anyone.
He suffered as much as anyone.

note: Fixed comparative; also tan … como el que más.

title: Está que arde: fuming, or things are heated

forms.es: Mi mamá está que echa chispas.

note: estar que + verb = intensified state. Natural across LatAm.

title: Me importa un comino.
es: Me importa un comino lo que digan.
note: For Spain's 'un pimiento'. Rude in formal settings — use 'me resulta indiferente'. Milder: '¡Qué más da!'.

title: A complete U-turn: dar un giro de 180 grados
es: La situación dio un giro de 180 grados.
note: Radical change of direction. 'Variar' = minor change; 'transformarse' = total change.

title: A diamond in the rough: un diamante en bruto
en: He's a diamond in the rough.

forms.en: He's a diamond in the rough.

note: 'En bruto' = before any refining; figuratively untapped talent (critics praising a newcomer). 'Al natural' = untreated.

title: Bone-chilling cold: un frío que cala los huesos
es: Hace un frío que cala (hasta) los huesos.
note: Replaces Peninsular 'un frío que pela' (dropped). Bogotá classic.

title: Just around the corner: a la vuelta de la esquina
es: La tienda está a la vuelta de la esquina. Diciembre está a la vuelta de la esquina.
en: just around the corner (place or time)
note: Literal and temporal.

title: Red-hot (tension): al rojo vivo
es: La discusión está al rojo vivo.
note: Literal (metal) and figurative (tension).

title: Any minute now: de un momento a otro
es: Llega de un momento a otro.
en: She'll be here any minute now.
note: Imminent — the opposite end from 'a la larga'.

title: Soaked to the skin: quedé ensopado
es: Me agarró el aguacero y quedé ensopado.
en: I got caught in the downpour and got soaked.

forms.es: Me agarró el aguacero y quedé ensopado.
forms.en: I got caught in the downpour and got soaked.

forms.es: Me agarró el aguacero y quedé hecho una sopa.
forms.en: I got caught in the downpour and got soaked to the skin.

note: Replaces Peninsular 'ponerse como una sopa'. 'Ensopado' (Col./Ven.) and 'hecho una sopa' are both natural; 'aguacero' = downpour.

title: A simple vista and al ojo
en: At a glance it looks new.

forms.en: At a glance it looks new.
I worked it out by eye.

note: 'Al ojo' is LatAm for Spain's 'a ojo'. Also 'por un pelo' (by the skin of your teeth), 'de antemano', 'a la larga', 'cuatro gatos'. Also 'con lujo de detalles' (Spain 'con pelos y señales').

title: Costing a fortune: cuesta un platal
note: Colombian/Ecuadorian for 'un dineral' (Spain 'una millonada'). Plata = money.

title: Colombian time: la hora colombiana
es: Llegó a la hora colombiana, una hora tarde.
en: He arrived on Colombian time, an hour late.
note: Self-ironic cultural phrase; pairs with Spain's stereotype 'puntualidad británica' (recognition).

title: Butterfingers: tiene manos de mantequilla
note: Replaces Peninsular 'ser un manazas' for dropping things. Widely used in Mexico and Colombia.

title: Scraping through: pasé raspando
en: I barely scraped through the exam.
note: Colombian student slang for passing by the minimum; 'por un pelo' is the pan-Hispanic option.

title: Handyman: es todero
es: Mi papá es todero: arregla de todo.
en: My dad's a real handyman: he fixes everything.
note: Replaces Peninsular 'ser un manitas'. Colombian; 'el todero' is also the job.

title: All the time: a cada rato
en: He calls me all the time.
note: Very common LatAm; 'a cada nada' is also mentioned in the source as Hispanoamerican — recognition.

title: In the middle of nowhere: donde el diablo perdió el poncho
es: Vive donde el diablo perdió el poncho.
en: He lives in the back of beyond.
note: LatAm (Andean/Southern Cone) equivalent of Spain's 'en el quinto pino'. Colombians also say 'queda en la Cochinchina' or 'en la loma del culo' (vulgar — recognition only).

title: A total mess: ¡qué despelote!
note: Colombian colloquial for 'un lío / un caos' — story dialogue / recognition.

title: Any old how: a la topa tolondra
es: Hizo el trabajo a la topa tolondra.
en: He did the job any old how.
note: Colombian: carelessly/hastily (cf. 'descuidado'). Story dialogue / recognition.

title: ¡Faltaba más!
en:
Will you help me?
Of course!
note: LatAm 'faltaba más' (Spain 'faltaría más'). Also 'Eso ni se pregunta' for obvious permission.

title: No te hubieras molestado.
note: LatAm form of 'No tenías que haberte molestado'. Thanks, not a reproach. Also '¿Qué haría yo sin ti?'.

title: ¿Qué es de tu vida?
en: What have you been up to all this time?
note: Only after a long time apart. Formal: 'Es un placer saludarlo después de tanto tiempo'.

title: Allá tú.
es: Allá tú, pero abrígate, que hace frío.
note: Warning (concern) or threat (resentment) depending on what follows. Paisa voseo 'allá vos' — recognition (unit 59). Pair: 'Luego no digas que no te avisé.'

title: ¿Me sigues? or ¿No te enredé?
es: ¿Me sigues, o te enredé con tanto detalle?
en: Are you following me, or have I lost you with all this detail?
note: LatAm 'enredar' for Spain's 'liar'. Different checks: following the thread vs. confused by a point.

title: Mil disculpas.
note: LatAm prefers 'mil disculpas' to Spain's 'mil perdones'. Reply with conditions: 'Por esta vez te la paso, pero que no se repita.'

title: No te voy a decir que no.
es: ¿Un tinto? No te voy a decir que no.
note: ACCEPTS through double negation. Also '¿Qué esperamos?' (enthusiastic) and 'Otra vez será' (refusal).

title: ¿Te animas? or ¿Te le mides?
es: Vamos a cine el viernes, ¿te animas?
en: We're going to the cinema on Friday, are you in?
note: LatAm for Spain's '¿Te apuntas?'. '¿Te le mides?' is Colombian (dare/up for it) — story dialogue. Pressure invite: 'No puedes faltar / No te lo puedes perder'; soften with 'No sé qué planes tengas, pero…'.

title: Bueno, te dejo.
es: Bueno, te dejo, que me están llamando por la otra línea.
note: Closing with a reason. Also '¡En fin!' and topic shifts 'A propósito de…', 'En otro orden de cosas'.

title: Sin ir más lejos…
es: Sin ir más lejos, esta misma mañana lo hablé con él.
en: Without looking any further, I talked it over with him this very morning.
note: Introduces an immediate, close-to-hand example.

title: To perfection: a la perfección
es: Interpretó el papel a la perfección.
en: She played the part to perfection.

title: Booming: en pleno auge
es: La escena musical de Bogotá está en pleno auge.
note: 'En pleno' also: en pleno centro, en plena crisis.

title: Finger-licking good: para chuparse los dedos
es: Este ajiaco está para chuparse los dedos.
note: Colloquial; pan-Hispanic.
